transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-10-07
Time: 10:00 AM PT
Duration: 45 minutes
Attendees: Samir Patel (Redwood AE), Laura Kim (Redwood SE), Diego Ramos (Redwood SE), Ethan Park (NovaScale CTO), Maya Gonzalez (ML Eng), Alex Li (Infra), Priya Sharma (Security)

Summary (auto): Weekly POC sync for Redwood Private (VPC pilot). Covered perf numbers, routing problems seen in cross-region tests, and the recent agent/kernel upgrade. Decided next steps and owners.

00:00 Samir: All right, good morning everyone, thanks for hopping on. Quick roll call, then we'll go through last week's items and the test results.
00:15 Ethan: Hey, Ethan here. Maya and Alex on my side.
00:20 Maya: Maya here.
00:26 Alex: Alex joining.
00:30 Samir: Great. Laura, do you want to kick off with the perf recap?
00:36 Laura: Yeah sure, so we ran the two-week run of the 95/99 latency tests across the east-west region pairing, the headline is median token latency improved about 8% after the agent upgrade, but we're still seeing tail spikes around 99th at peak load when burst capacity is hit. The KV cash priming helped some but not enough during simultaneous long-sequence requests.
01:05 Maya: When you say agent upgrade, is that the kernel change from 1.9 to 2.0 or the runtime patch? I think we applied the runtime patch on Tuesday.
01:14 Laura: Good point, it's the runtime agent 2.0 which bundles a few kernel selection tweaks — kernel selection changes and a batching heuristic update. The kernel change is the one that seems to cut median latency; the tail still looks like routing and packet drops on the peering link.
01:36 Alex: We saw some retransmits on our side, yes, at around 2200 UTC on Tuesday which corresponded to a batch of failed handshakes on the VPC peering. I think there's a transient MTU mismatch on one of the TGWs.
01:56 Diego: That would cause fragmentation and some packets drop under load; which could explain the 99 spikes. Did you confirm iptables or firewall rules changing?
02:08 Alex: We haven't changed iptables recently; we did a subnet resize last month but that shouldn't affect the MTU per se. I'll pull the logs.
02:17 Samir: Okay action item for Alex to pull the VPC peering and TGW logs and share with Laura and Diego.
02:25 Alex: Yep I'll do that.

04:00 Laura: On the KV cache side, the priming script we used warmed about 70% of prefixes before the run. With a full priming we expect a further 6-9% throughput improvement but it'll add about 20 minutes to the prep window. Tradeoff there.
04:26 Maya: For production we won't have full priming every time; can we do incremental priming or a prioritized prefix list so the top 10% of calls are always primed?
04:36 Laura: Yes, prioritized priming is doable — we can produce a hot-prefix list based on your traffic distribution. We'll share the script and parameters.

07:10 Priya: Quick security note — we've got to ensure audit logs are captured for all inference calls, and that they're stored in your KMS-backed bucket. Any changes to logging pathway after the VPC peering could affect the chain.
07:26 Samir: Right, Redwood Private already supports forwarding audit logs to your S3 via VPC endpoints and KMS encryption; we'll share the configuration we used in the pilot.
07:36 Priya: Also SAML/SSO metadata — we'll need the exact issuer and cert.
07:40 Samir: We'll include that in the configuration doc.

09:05 Ethan: Can we talk about routing? We noticed that some requests route to the regional fallback in us-west during spikes, which increases cross-region latency. That should not happen for pinned sessions.
09:20 Laura: That's likely the smart routing policy falling back when a capacity group reports saturated. We have a couple knob settings: stricter affinity (pin sessions to a pool) vs allowing fallback to cheapest region. For the pilot we left fallback enabled to test resilience.
09:39 Ethan: We want stronger affinity — commercial product needs pinned sessions for compliance and consistent latency.
09:46 Samir: Understood. For the pilot we can change the route policy to strict-affinity; Laura can also lower the fallback timeout so it doesn't trigger prematurely.
09:58 Laura: Note though that strict-affinity increases the chance of queueing if pool is full — so you'll need to provision dedicated capacity or allow a small burst window. We can show tradeoffs with a quick cost/latency table.

12:15 Diego: On the agent side, we noticed the new kernel selection logic favors smaller sequence-optimized kernels which helps short conversations but on long context it sometimes chooses a slower kernel causing the tail to degrade. We can force a kernel mapping for long-seq models.
12:33 Maya: We're using a 32k-context model for some batch jobs; that might be the trigger.
12:40 Laura: Right, for 32k contexts the current heuristic underestimates memory pressure in the combined KV cache + batching scenario. We can pin the kernel map for that model in your pilot config.
12:51 Diego: We'll prepare a pinned-kernel config and test.

15:02 Samir: Any issues with upgrades? We did a rolling upgrade last Sunday across the pilot and there were a couple of nodes that did not drain cleanly. We observed some 502 spikes while they were rebooting.
15:15 Ethan: We saw a small outage window, maybe 2 minutes, when a node didn't rejoin and traffic was routed to fallback. That aligns with our audit.
15:24 Laura: The rolling upgrade script has a stricter drain check patch in the next release; we can stage that into your environment before the next upgrade.
15:34 Samir: We'll run it in canary on two nodes first.

18:00 Alex: Regarding network MTU, I pulled the TGW logs — there's an inconsistent MTU on the customer transit GW cluster in eu-west which is causing fragmentation when we cross to us-east — but the major issue is the path over the partner transit where PMTU discovery is blocked by a firewall rule (ICMP blocked).
18:22 Priya: We intentionally block some ICMP for security, but we can open specific ICMP types for PMTU.
18:30 Alex: If we allow 3-4 ICMP types between the two TGWs the PMTU will settle and fragmentation should go away.
18:39 Samir: Action item: Priya to share current firewall rules, Alex to try temporarily opening the PMTU ICMP types and rerun the cross-region test.

21:10 Maya: On workload side, do you recommend smaller batches or larger batches for throughput? We saw better tokens/sec with larger batching but worse tail for long sequences.
21:25 Laura: For your mix (50% short, 50% long), we recommend hybrid batching: small max batch for long-seq model types and dynamic batching for short ones. Also use KV cache warm to avoid repeated decode cost.
21:44 Diego: We'll propose a batching profile YAML we used in other pilots — Samir will share that.

24:00 Ethan: Cost concerns — if we switch to strict-affinity and reserve more capacity, what's the delta? We need rough numbers for budgeting.
24:13 Samir: We'll produce a cost delta table — rough estimate is 20-35% increase on committed monthly spend for strict-affinity with a 20% headroom. Exact numbers depend on concurrency targets. We'll include a sample spreadsheet.
24:30 Ethan: Okay please send that.

27:05 Laura: Quick note about audit log retention: Redwood can push logs to your S3 with lifecycle rules; if you need SOC2 retention of 7 years that's doable but will affect storage and cost.
27:20 Priya: For now we just need 2 years in hot storage and long term in cold. We'll work with billing.

30:00 Samir: Let's recap next steps. I have: send routing design and cost delta; Laura has: KV cache script and priming params plus batching profile; Alex will run MTU test after firewall change; Priya will share firewall rules and SAML metadata; NovaScale will run 1k concurrent benchmark.
30:22 Ethan: One more ask — can Redwood share a trimmed-down benchmark harness so we can reproduce your harness locally?
30:32 Laura: Yes we can share the harness and the traffic generator configs. We'll put it in the shared folder and note env vars to change.
30:41 Maya: Please include the seed prompts and the tokenization script so we match token counts.
30:48 Laura: Will do.

33:00 Diego: A couple of small notes: we recommend enabling the newer batcher flag which reduces small-batch latency for short requests — non-breaking. We'll provide the flag name and rollout instructions.
33:16 Samir: We'll include the rollout steps in the doc.

35:30 Alex: Regarding logs, there was a missing trace id on a few error entries — are you adding trace propagation in the next agent build?
35:38 Laura: Yes trace propagation is in the next build, should be in the canary. We'll tag the canary and provide the build id.

38:10 Priya: For the SOC2 deep-dive, can we schedule an hour with your compliance engineer? We want to review encryption at rest, KMS key rotation, and audit completeness.
38:24 Samir: Absolutely. I'll introduce you to our compliance contact and propose dates next week.

40:50 Ethan: Anything else? I think that's it from our side.
40:55 Samir: Thanks everyone. We'll follow up with the docs and schedule. Next sync same time next week unless we need an ad-hoc.
41:05 Maya: Works for me.
41:08 Alex: Works.
41:10 End of transcript.
